weeks.title: Orthography, Syllable Quantities & The Zero-Copula Nominal Clause

chapters.title: Orthography, Phonetics & Syllable Quantity
chapters.textbookTitle: The Arabic Language. Orthography. Phonetics. Punctuation
chapters.classicalFocus: The 28 consonants; long and short vowels; auxiliary signs (sukūn, shaddah, maddah); distinction between hamzat al-qaṭʿ (disjunctive) and hamzat al-waṣl (elidable) essential for Qur'anic reading.
coreRules: Solar letters (ḥurūf shamsiyyah) assimilate the lām of al-; lunar letters (qamariyyah) retain it.
Hamzat al-waṣl elides in connected recitation while hamzat al-qaṭʿ is always pronounced.
chapters.practiceFocus: Reading vowelled text and tracking hamzat al-waṣl across connected phrases.

chapters.title: The Definite Article & The Nominal Sentence
chapters.textbookTitle: The Article. The Simple Nominal Sentence
chapters.classicalFocus: Structure of the equational nominal sentence (al-jumlah al-ismiyyah): Subject (al-mubtadaʾ) and Predicate (al-khabar); zero-copula syntax in the present tense.
coreRules: Indefiniteness is marked by nunation (tanwīn); prefixing al- removes tanwīn.
The mubtadaʾ is typically definite and nominative; the khabar agrees in gender and number.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 1–2: parsing mubtadaʾ and khabar in simple equational clauses.

chapters.title: Gender & Collective Nouns of Unity
chapters.classicalFocus: Markers of the feminine (principally tāʾ marbūṭah ة); nouns feminine by meaning or convention; collective nouns (ism al-jins) and nouns of unity (ism al-waḥdah).
coreRules: Adjectives and predicates agree in grammatical gender with feminine and collective nouns.
Interrogative particles a- and hal introduce yes/no questions.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 3–4: identifying inherent feminines and gender agreement.

chapters.title: The Three Cases (Aḥwāl al-Iʿrāb)
chapters.textbookTitle: Declension of Nouns. The Three Cases
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 3 (§3.9, Case and Mood) & Ch. 8 (The Case System, §§8.1–8.4)
chapters.classicalFocus: Threefold declension: Nominative (rafʿ with ḍammah), Accusative (naṣb with fatḥah), and Genitive (jarr with kasrah); nunation (tanwīn) and accusative alif.
coreRules: Indefinite accusative singular takes a trailing alif (ـًا), except on tāʾ marbūṭah and hamzah after alif.
Prepositions (ḥurūf al-jarr) govern the following noun in the genitive case.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 5–6: identifying case endings on definite and indefinite substantives and vocalizing governing prepositions.

weeks.title: Duals, Sound Plurals & Broken Plurals I

chapters.title: Number — Duals, Sound Plurals & Personal Pronouns
chapters.textbookTitle: Number. The Sound Masculine and Feminine Plurals. Some Simple Verb Forms
chapters.classicalFocus: Singular (mufrad), Dual (muthannā in -āni / -ayni), and Sound Plurals; inflection through letters (iʿrāb bi-l-ḥurūf) rather than short vowels.
coreRules: Duals inflect by letter (-āni nom., -ayni acc./gen.).
Sound masculine plurals take -ūna / -īna; sound feminine plurals take -ātun / -ātin.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 7–8: inflecting duals and sound plurals across all three cases.

chapters.title: The Triliteral Root System & Broken Plurals I
chapters.classicalFocus: The radical root system (al-aṣl al-thulāthī) and the metric exemplar pattern f-ʿ-l (ف-ع-ل); broken plurals (jamʿ al-taksīr) and non-human plural agreement.
coreRules: Non-human broken plurals are grammatically treated as feminine singular for adjective and verb agreement.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 9–10: root pattern deduction (wazn) and pairing broken plurals with feminine singular modifiers.

weeks.title: Advanced Broken Plurals & The Annexation Construct (Al-Iḍāfah)

chapters.title: Advanced Broken Plurals
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 7 (The Broken Plural, quadriliteral patterns)
chapters.classicalFocus: Advanced broken plural patterns including quadriliteral patterns (faʿālil, faʿālīl).
coreRules: Quadriliteral plural patterns faʿālil and faʿālīl are diptotes (no tanwīn).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 11–12: pattern recognition and root extraction.

chapters.title: The Genitive Construct (Al-Iḍāfah)
chapters.classicalFocus: Al-muḍāf (stripped of tanwīn and al-) and al-muḍāf ilayh (strictly majrūr); multi-tiered construct chains; true vs. adjectival annexation.
coreRules: The muḍāf never takes al- or tanwīn and drops the final nūn of duals and sound masculine plurals.
The muḍāf ilayh is always in the genitive case (majrūr).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 13–14: parsing possessive chains in theological and Qur'anic phrases (e.g., Bayt Allāh, Yawm al-Dīn).

chapters.title: The Attached Pronouns (Al-Ḍamāʾir al-Muttaṣilah)
chapters.classicalFocus: Attached enclitic pronouns suffixed to nouns (possession/genitive) and prepositions (pronominal objects); phonological vowel shifts.
coreRules: Third-person suffixes (-hu / -hum) shift to -hi / -him following kasrah or yāʾ.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 15–16: parsing pronominal suffixes on prepositions and particles.

chapters.title: Demonstrative Pronouns (Asmāʾ al-Ishārah)
chapters.classicalFocus: Near demonstratives (hādhā / hādhihi) and distant demonstratives (dhālika / tilka); phrase vs. complete clause syntax.
coreRules: Demonstrative + noun with al- forms a noun phrase (hādhā l-kitābu); demonstrative + indefinite noun forms a complete nominal sentence (hādhā kitābun).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 17–18: distinguishing demonstrative phrases from equational clauses.

weeks.title: Adjectival Concordance & Form I Past Verb

chapters.title: Adjectival Concordance & Elatives
chapters.classicalFocus: Fourfold adjectival agreement (gender, number, case, definiteness); comparative and superlative patterns (ism al-tafḍīl on afʿal).
coreRules: An attributive adjective follows its noun and matches it in gender, number, case, and definiteness.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 19–20: adjectival phrases and elative constructions.

chapters.title: The Verb — Form I Past Verb (Al-Fiʿl al-Māḍī)
chapters.classicalFocus: Form I base verb (al-fiʿl al-mujarrad); stem vowel variations (faʿala, faʿila, faʿula); full 13-person paradigm; V-S-O verbal syntax.
coreRules: A verb preceding an overt plural subject remains singular and agrees only in gender.
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 21–22: conjugating sound Form I verbs and analyzing V-S-O word order.

weeks.title: Pronominal Direct Objects & Auxiliary Copular Verbs (Kāna)

chapters.title: Pronominal Direct Objects & Kāna wa-Akhawātuhā
chapters.textbookTitle: The Verb with Pronominal Object. The Verb "to be"
chapters.rydingReference: Ryding Ch. 21 (§21.2, Verb Strings) & Ch. 36 (Verbs of Being: Kāna wa-Akhawātuhā)
chapters.classicalFocus: Pronominal object clitics on verbs (-nī, -ka, -hu, -hā, -nā); defective auxiliary verb kāna and its grammatical governance.
coreRules: Ism kāna remains nominative (marfūʿ), while khabar kāna is obligatorily inflected in the accusative (manṣūb).
chapters.practiceFocus: Haywood & Nahmad Exercises 23–24: identifying verb objects vs. noun suffixes and vocalizing kāna clauses.

chapters.title: Module 1 Consolidation & Early Supplement Iʿrāb
chapters.classicalFocus: Comprehensive synthesis of nominal syntax, case endings, iḍāfah, pronouns, and Form I past verbs.
coreRules: Read aloud and parse the iʿrāb of unvocalized nominal and verbal sentences, naming every case ending and governing factor (ʿāmil).
chapters.practiceFocus: Synthesis exercise on early sections of Haywood & Nahmad Literary Supplement (p. 462).
